entries.title: Google Play unveils the best apps, games, and books of 2026
entries.summary: Gold and yellow promotional graphic with diagonal stripes displaying the text "Best of 2026", next to a sleek, modern 3D trophy featuring the multi-colored Google Play logo
entries.content:
Today, we’re sharing the winners of our annual Best of Play awards — and celebrating the incredible creativity, passion, and technical polish that developers bring to our screens. Google Play is defined by the achievements of the developers and publishers who build for it. These awards are designed to put their outstanding work front and center, both on and off the store.

This year's winners showcase a major shift in how people interact with their devices, reflecting a deeper need for technology that’s both highly efficient and genuinely supportive. In apps, developers are building intelligent, ambient tools that automate daily tasks, shifting the ecosystem from demanding our attention to quietly giving us back our time. In games, studios continue to weave rich narratives into core gameplay, but at a larger scale, with optimizations that let players jump between phones, tablets, and PCs.

This digital creativity is matched by the authors and publishers behind this year's greatest books and audiobooks.

We’re grateful for the developers and publishers whose energy and ideas make technology more enjoyable for people around the world.

Read on for the full list of award winners in the U.S. You can also see all the winners on the Best of 2026 page on Play, and read about the local winners in Asia Pacific.

Best overall app and game

Best App: Notability: AI & PDF Notes

Notability is a digital notebook for learning, work, and productivity that both professionals and students will appreciate. Now natively built for Android, it turns your device into an AI-powered workspace to chat with materials, create study organizers, generate custom quizzes, and streamline workflows.

Best Game: Arknights: Endfield

From its story to its vibrant vistas, every inch of Arknights: Endfield has us hooked. With slick real-time combat, rich characters, and deep factory-building and management mechanics, it offers a truly unique experience we won't soon forget.

Best cross-device app and game

Best Cross-device App: Strava: Run, Bike, Walk

Strava harmonizes our entire fitness routine across screens. We enjoyed the seamlessness it brought to logging reps hands-free on a Wear OS watch and checking weekly progress at a glance on a lock screen widget.

Best Cross-device Game: Moonlight Peaks

Whether we were tending to magical crops or wooing werewolves, Moonlight Peaks had us embracing the simple life this year. We loved catching up on the latest town gossip while we were on the go — and settling in with Google Play Games on PC or on Googlebook for longer sessions.

  • Best Innovative App: Wispr Flow: AI Voice-to-Text
  • Best for Creative Expression: ibis Paint X
  • Best for Skill Building: Spark: Daily Learning Puzzles

  • Best Under the Radar: Riley : Emotion & Mood Tracker
  • Best for Kids and Families: Superfonik: Kids Learn to Read
  • Best for Watches: Pocket Casts - Podcast App
  • Best for Large Screens: BandLab: Music Maker & Studio
  • Best for Cars: Audible: Audiobooks & Podcasts
  • Best for XR: MLB
  • Top Trending: Vinted: Shop & sell pre-loved; Pocket FM: Audio Dramas; FotMob - Soccer Live Scores

Best games of 2026

  • Best Multiplayer: Warframe
  • Best Pick Up & Play: Subway Surfers City
  • Best Indie: Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor
  • Best Story: Sea of Stars
  • Best Ongoing: Zenless Zone Zero

entries.title: The best of Google Play in Asia Pacific
entries.summary: Google Play Best of 2026 app icons
entries.content:
Today, we’re celebrating Google Play’s Best of 2026 awards, recognizing outstanding apps and games that helped people learn, play, and get things done this year. Among the winners, developers across Asia Pacific are standing out on the world stage, with everything from console-grade games that can be played across devices to apps that are simplifying daily life.

Here’s a closer look at the trends that shaped this year’s winners.

Gaming across screens

APAC developers set new benchmarks for visual quality and game depth without compromising mobile performance. China’s Gryphline secured “Best Game” globally excluding Japan and Korea with Arknights: Endfield, an ambitious title that combines action-RPG combat with complex factory-automation systems. NTE: Neverness to Everness from China's Perfect World took “Best Cross-device Game” in many markets, with players saying they love its smooth transition between PC and mobile screens.

Connecting through local culture

Leaning into regional nuance and fan culture, APAC developers delivered standout hits tailored to local audiences. In Japan, hololive Dreams secured “Best Game” by tapping into the oshikatsu fan culture, offering custom VTuber theme park experiences. LINE Music (“Best for Entertainment” in Japan) let fans curate their oshi with a “My Oshi” feature.

Hyper-local settings also resonated in 2026. Scarfall 2.0 by Blast+ Games claimed “Best Made in India” with a 100-player Mumbai map built around local trains and city streets. Own Games' Tukang Sate VS Ojol Rush won “Best Made in Indonesia” by turning street food and rideshare culture into casual fun. DramaBox (“Best Entertainment App” in Hong Kong and Taiwan) capitalized on the APAC-first short-drama trend, and Pocket FM (“Best Entertainment App” in India) helped people create audio content.

This year’s winners also included long-running titles with player-friendly updates. HoYoverse won “Best Ongoing Game” in the Americas and European markets for Zenless Zone Zero, while NEXON tapped into two decades of nostalgia with MapleStory: Idle RPG, a new entry in the series that earned “Best Game” in Korea.

Simplifying with smart tools

People across APAC found new ways to make life easier on Google Play this year. Nutrition tracker Asken won “Best App” in Japan, thanks to its AI-powered nutritional feedback and meal suggestions. Convenience took center stage in India, where quick-commerce app Pronto was named “Best Productivity Partner” for arranging household help in minutes.

Content consumption also evolved in 2026. PowerDirector (“Best App” in Hong Kong and “Best Cross-device App” in Japan) simplified editing across screens, Korea’s Cuts Make (“Best App”) turned static webtoons into dynamic short videos, and Vidio (“Best for Entertainment” in Indonesia) used AI to create clips of sporting events within minutes of on-pitch activity. Indonesian sports fans had more to enjoy in the AYO: Super Sport Community App, (“Best for Sports Fans” in Indonesia) digital clubhouse. And language learners got a gamified narrative experience with Korea’s Ssadaboca (“Best Under the Radar”).

Find the full list of Best of 2026 winners on the Google Play Store.

entries.title: Celebrate 100 years of Colonial Williamsburg online
entries.summary: A costumed historical interpreter holding a document up high follows a group of musicians in 18th-century attire along a road, facing a large crowd gathered in front of Colonial Williamsburg’s Capitol building.
entries.content:
Today, as Colonial Williamsburg marks its 100th anniversary, Google Arts & Culture is sharing new immersive stories and newly digitized cultural artifacts that honor a century of preservation, discovery, and public access. These additions expand on the digital hub we launched earlier this year with The Colonial Williamsburg Foundation to celebrate America’s 250th birthday and bring the rich history of early America online.

Discover the latest stories and archives

We’re introducing three new ways to explore Colonial Williamsburg’s legendary collections, taking you behind the scenes of how history is preserved, studied, and brought to life.

  • Step inside an immersive online gallery: Learn about the Historic Area’s restoration, which began in 1926. This interactive gallery pairs rare archival photos with modern photography and period music across the first three reconstructed sites: the Governor’s Palace, the Raleigh Tavern, and the Capitol.
  • Browse more than 3,000 new digital records: Through our ongoing collaboration, a specialized high-resolution tabletop scanner has helped digitize tightly bound volumes, delicate manuscripts, and centuries-old records. Today, we’re launching over 3,000 newly scanned images — including rare issues of the Virginia Gazette, fragile archival records, and special collections assets — making many of these treasures accessible to the public online for the very first time.
  • Read new stories celebrating 100 years: New immersive stories capture the breadth of Colonial Williamsburg’s work and collections. Ranging from rare natural history surveys and early newspapers to reproductions and everyday items, these narratives explore the complex tapestry of American history through the experiences of ordinary people and the vital legacies of historically marginalized voices — and showcase the behind-the-scenes work keeping their histories alive.

Step into the kitchen with Max Miller’s “Tasting History”

In partnership with Colonial Williamsburg and YouTube, culinary historian Max Miller, creator of “Tasting History,” visited the living history museum to film an exclusive episode, bringing 18th-century traditions to life. Praising the museum’s meticulous historical accuracy, Miller worked alongside Ivey Boyd, chef de cuisine at the King’s Arms Tavern, to prepare snow eggs (oeufs à la neige). This French dessert was popularized in early America by James Hemings, Thomas Jefferson's enslaved chef, and is served today at Colonial Williamsburg. This collaboration bridges traditional preservation with modern storytelling, inviting a new generation to discover the flavors and stories of early America.

Look ahead to the next century of access

By expanding access to Colonial Williamsburg’s collections, we’re safeguarding centuries-old treasures while sharing their history with the world. As Colonial Williamsburg enters its second century, we invite you to experience these new stories, archival records, and the living history of early America in a whole new way.

Explore The Colonial Williamsburg Foundation on Google Arts & Culture today.

entries.title: Regional voices are rolling out in the Gemini app.
entries.summary: Gemini now offers 66 regional voices on Android and iOS. Choose a natural, local dialect for your app interactions. Pick your favorite voice today.
entries.content:
At Google I/O, we shared plans to bring local dialects to Gemini, so you can choose a voice that truly resonates with you. Today, we’re rolling out 66 new regional voices in the Gemini app on Android and iOS, including U.S. English, U.K. English, India English, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese, Indonesian, and Korean, with tailored options for each.

Each voice is tuned for natural cadences and everyday clarity, rather than exaggerated accents. They capture familiar local rhythms, pitch, and inflection to make talking with Gemini feel more personal. Your selected voice carries across the entire app, whether you’re brainstorming out loud in Gemini Live, practicing a language, or tapping the Listen icon in chat to hear a detailed response read aloud.

To preview the new options and pick a favorite, tap the three-dot menu in Gemini Live, or open Gemini’s voice in your app settings.

entries.title: The era of autonomous attacks has arrived.
entries.summary: See how bad actors are shifting to autonomous attacks and how Google AI Threat Defense uses Gemini to defend against them.
entries.content:
Imagine a hacker that doesn’t eat, sleep, or get tired, and never stops searching for a way in.

According to the latest AI Threat Tracker report, bad actors are now using autonomous LLM frameworks to continuously scan software updates, figure out what flaw was patched, and build an attack for it — all without human involvement.

Defending against machine-speed threats at human speed isn’t feasible. That's why we're helping defenders rethink security in the agentic era with Google AI Threat Defense, which combines Gemini and other frontier models, Wiz’s context and prioritization, CodeMender’s automated patching, and Mandiant’s expertise to continuously find and fix flaws before attackers can exploit them.

Read the full report on the Google Cloud Threat Intelligence blog.

entries.title: New Google AdMob AI tools help app creators build, fix, and grow faster
entries.summary: Introducing Ask AdMob, with various example prompts
entries.content:
Building a successful mobile app means balancing a great user experience with ads monetization. But manually managing ad setups, fixing integration errors, and auditing brand safety pulls your team’s focus away from building. To help you simplify operations and accelerate your productivity, we’re introducing new AI tools for AdMob, Ask AdMob, agent skills and an MCP server. These new tools, built with Google AI, can help you earn more revenue and build your app business faster.

Fine-tune your monetization with Ask AdMob

Ask AdMob, a conversational agent built with Gemini, will live directly in your AdMob account. Trained on AdMob monetization best practices, it can help fix issues, find revenue opportunities, and protect your brand safety like an AdMob product expert. Here are a few examples of what Ask AdMob can do for you.

Find and fix setup issues, skipping the manual guesswork: The troubleshooting hub will help you spot setup anomalies and SDK integration issues. Ask AdMob has visibility into how ads are loading in your app so it can highlight recommendations to resolve issues impacting your revenue.

Identify new revenue opportunities: Ask AdMob uses peer benchmarks to recommend high-value SDK bidders with predicted revenue uplifts to add to your setup and help optimize your mediation groups. For example, Ask AdMob will automatically check your third-party network configuration to catch costly typos and floor price discrepancies before they impact your yield.

  • Create effective brand safety rules with natural language: Instead of manually managing blocklists, you can configure custom brand safety rules using simple, natural-language prompts in your AdMob UI.

We’ll begin testing these capabilities over the next few months and continue evolving Ask AdMob with more advanced features to take action on your behalf later next year. As always, you remain in control, reviewing and approving every recommendation before it’s applied.

Manage ad setups directly with your AI agent

Previously, setting up ad placements meant clicking through web dashboards, copying and pasting ad unit IDs, and managing ad configuration files outside your codebase. With AdMob agent skills and an upcoming MCP server, we’re giving you the tools to enable your preferred AI agent to build, edit, and validate ad code for your app.

AdMob agent skills give your AI agent pre-built, tested playbooks to implement coding tasks like, migrating to the Google Mobile Ads Next-Gen SDK, validating your SDK implementation, and implementing new ad formats in your app. Find these skills and more on our developer site.

While agent skills can help you implement tasks today, we’re also working on an AdMob MCP server to connect your developer environments directly with AdMob. Soon your AI agent will be able to read account data, write new ad units, and manage mediation settings. All you have to do is review and approve the updates before you push them to production. This is in early testing and will be expanding to more developers early next year.

Prepare your business for a more agentic 2027

Throughout 2027, we’ll introduce a much broader and more advanced wave of AI tools for app developers — expanding both in-product and AI agent capabilities. These tools will handle more of the routine operational workload so you can focus on what matters most: your product, your users, and your business.

entries.title: New AI training performance benchmarks for Google TPUs
entries.summary: In the latest MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark round, Google Cloud published 10 results across seventh-generation Ironwood TPUs and NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs, spanning f…
entries.content:
In the latest MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark round 1 , Google Cloud published 10 results across seventh-generation Ironwood TPUs and NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs, spanning frontier pre-training and the first MLPerf benchmark for agentic reinforcement learning (RL). Built on Google Cloud’s AI Hypercomputer architecture, these results reflect co-design across silicon, networking, and open software:

  • Pre-training on Ironwood: 8,192 Ironwood TPUs reached the target model's benchmark target quality in 1.70 minutes, scaling up to 4,096 chips with 96% efficiency.
  • Agentic RL on Ironwood: 640 Ironwood TPUs reached the target model’s coding benchmark target accuracy in 18.02 minutes (0.765 vs. the 0.69 goal), running code generation and learning simultaneously so training chips waited under 3% of the time.
  • NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs: On Google Cloud A4X Max Instances, 256 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs for pre-training benchmark reached the target quality in 31.96 minutes, complemented by five A4X and A4X Max submissions on the agentic RL benchmark.

For more details on the MLPerf Training v6.1 results, click here.

entries.title: Transform notes, research, and sources into interactive sites with Gemini Notebook.
entries.summary: Gemini Notebook now turns your research into interactive sites. Build project trackers and visual dashboards with Google. Create your site today.
entries.content:
Starting today, Gemini Notebook can turn your sources into interactive sites to help you quickly make sense of complex information.

To get started, simply type “make me a site” in your Gemini Notebook chat along with a description of what you want to build for work or study, such as:

  • Visual explainers to help you prepare for exams, like an interactive periodic table or a historical timeline.
  • Interactive dashboards to explore your data, such as quarterly sales performance.
  • Project management trackers to outline your tasks and deadlines.

Once built, select “Open in a new tab” to interact with it, or share it with others.

This capability is rolling out globally on the web today for Gemini Notebook users (18+), including Google Workspace subscribers, and is coming soon to the mobile app.

entries.title: How to find the best Black Friday deals and shop smarter
entries.summary: Collage of various holiday shopping products
entries.content:
Between flash sales, doorbusters, and dozens of open browser tabs, holiday deal-hunting can take up all your time. Our shopping features are here to lend a hand, helping you save time and money. Here are four ways to snag the best deals and gifts this Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

1. Prep your wish list and snag deals with Universal Cart.

Universal Cart can act as your central game plan for Black Friday and Cyber Monday. Add items you’re eyeing across retailers into one organized place, Universal Cart will notify you about price drops or when out-of-stock items return. It also shows you merchant promo codes and offers.

The cart is built on Google Wallet so it understands your card perks and intelligently helps you choose between payment methods. When you’re ready to buy, check out securely right in the cart using Google Pay, or transfer your items to the retailer’s site to check out there.

2. Find gifts for anyone on your list with Search and the Gemini app.

Shopping for friends and family who have niche hobbies or never share a wishlist can leave you stuck for ideas. With AI Mode in Search or the Gemini app, just describe the person you’re shopping for in everyday language like “useful gifts under $40 for an uncle training for his first half marathon” to get tailored thought starters and gift ideas with customer reviews, photos, and store availability.

3. Shop with confidence using Price Insights.

Before you click “check out,” make sure you have the best deals out there. Tap the product listing on Google to compare prices across merchants and review price history to see whether the price is low, typical, or high. If you want to know when the price drops, tap “Track price” or ask AI Mode to let you know when there’s a deal.

4. Search in-store shelves using Google Lens.

If an item on a store shelf catches your eye, you do not have to guess what to type into Search to find it online. Just open up the Google app (Android and iOS), tap the Lens camera icon and snap a photo to instantly learn more about the product and see everything from customer reviews to product details to similar styles. You can even ask follow-up questions about what you see, like “does this come in navy blue?” or “what’s a great complimentary gift to go with this?”

With Google tools helping you tackle your holiday gift shopping, you can check your list off early and spend more time celebrating with family and friends.

entries.title: New Ask Maps features to help with holiday travel and prep
entries.content:
The holidays are a busy time between shopping for gifts, planning travel, and celebrating with loved ones. To help you stay one step ahead this season, we’re launching new Ask Maps features that make it easy to create itineraries, find available appointments, and search your lists in a snap so you can enjoy stress-free festivities.

Get on-the-go help with your holiday road trips

Now you can build step-by-step trip itineraries and get helpful, real-time details about your route right when you pull up directions.

Use Ask Maps to plan a day trip for holiday shopping or something more complex — like a three-day road trip with stops for coastal hikes and oceanfront dining. You'll get a day-by-day schedule with insider tips and numbered map pins for each stop, making it easy to visualize the plan. Once you're happy with the itinerary, share it with friends and family, or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

When you’re about to head out, use Ask Maps to pull up your itinerary or look for the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. You’ll see real-time details like live traffic conditions, whether a place is open, and even what the vibe is at your next stop. You can also adjust your schedule on the fly. Just use Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or lunch spot along the way. Then, tap to get directions to your next stop right from your itinerary.

Whether you're taking a multi-day road trip or running errands around town, Maps keeps you a step ahead. Pull up directions to see helpful “Know before you go” tips about your route, including where to park or charge your car, and real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Check off your holiday prep and let Maps find appointments for you

Holiday prep comes with a long list of to-dos. Now, with new agentic capabilities, you can choose to have Ask Maps find beauty, pet care, auto and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you. Just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me.” Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses so it’s easy to decide what to book.

Show your guests the best spots on your lists

If you have friends visiting and want to show them around, now you can use Ask Maps to find saved places on your lists in seconds. Just ask, “Which spots saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?” Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability so you can pick a place and go.

These updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS just in time for the holidays. As part of today’s news, Ask Maps starts expanding to 30 countries across Europe — including Spain, Germany, and the U.K. — bringing Ask Maps to more than 200 countries and territories globally.

Travel itineraries and list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know before you go" route tips and finding appointments are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.
